Google представила Gemini 4 Argon — новую флагманскую модель семейства Gemini, ориентированную на сложные многошаговые задачи.

retained_facts.text: Google представила Gemini 4 Argon — новую флагманскую модель семейства Gemini, ориентированную на сложные многошаговые задачи.
Главная особенность модели — возможность генерировать до 1 млн выходных токенов за один запрос, тогда как у предыдущего поколения этот предел составлял 64 000.
Google делает ставку на сценарии, в которых модель может долго работать над одной задачей, последовательно выполняя множество действий.
В другом проекте модель переработала 32 000 строк SIMD-кода: получившаяся версия на Rust, по данным Google, выполнялась в 2,7 раза быстрее предыдущего варианта.

Ещё один проект с несколькими агентами Argon помог найти способы оптимизации памяти в инфраструктуре компани, а после внедрения решений было высвобождено более 300 ТиБ оперативной памяти: потенциальный эффект Google оценивает в 500 ТиБ–1 ПиБ.
Argon способна самостоятельно искать уязвимости, проверять найденные проблемы и предлагать или осуществлять их исправление.

gemini.name: gemini/attempt_1/02 Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model
full_article_launch_sentences: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model Abner Li Sep 30 2026

retained_facts.text: Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s “next era of frontier intelligence” and built for “deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows.” It follows the cancellation of Gemini 3.5 Pro and focus on 3.8 Flash.
With this new model (which has a new naming scheme), Google wants to offer “frontier-level capabilities” across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity defense, and creative writing.
Gemini 4 Argon’s output token limit is 1M tokens (up from 64K) to allow for longer and more complex use cases.
This is paired with expanded coding, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities.
In terms of benchmarks, Google touts a DeepSWE v1.1 score of 77.9%.

“On AutomationBench, Zapier’s benchmark measuring end-to-end execution across core business functions, Argon ranks #1 with a score of 51.3%.” “…on LVBench, which measures long video understanding, Argon is state of the art with a score of 91.7%.”

gemini.name: gemini/attempt_1/03 Google pulls back the curtain to tease Gemini 4 Argon

retained_facts.text: Google's next-gen Gemini is coming soon — but you can't try it just yet.
Gemini 4 Argon is coming soon as Google’s most capable AI model to date.
Benchmarks show highly competitive scores across a wide range of agentic tasks.

New AI models drop so frequently, it’s difficult to even think of a week that’s not particularly packed with them, but these last few days have proven especially fruitful, giving us everything from Claude Sonnet 5.5 to GPT-6.1 Sol.
For a while now, we’d been wondering when Google would finally be ready to introduce the next big evolution of Gemini, and today the company finally starts outlining exactly what to expect.
Like many of the other flagship models we’re following, the improvements Google’s been prioritizing for Gemini 4 Argon aren’t just directly about the model’s raw performance.

gemini.name: gemini/attempt_1/04 Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful mod
full_article_launch_sentences: Google parent company Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing.

retained_facts.text: Google parent company Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing.
But it’s cybersecurity that Gemini 4 Argon is supposed to have a particular knack for, according to Google.
Argon is only being rolled out to a select group of the company’s cyber partners through its Fairwind Program, Google’s security initiative.
The model was trained specifically for defensive cyber work, and the company says it can “autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities.”

Argon is also said to be good at coding and engineering, with the company noting that its own staff have already been using the model for their daily work, including debugging and codebase migrations.
In its blog, Google claims that Argon scored significantly higher than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable and Opus models across a variety of AI benchmarks.

Vals Index оценивает экономическую пользу в финансах, коде, юриспруденции и налогах: 68,9% против 67% у Opus 5.5.

Google называет 77,9% новым рекордом (Opus 5.5 набрал 74,2%, Astra 74,1%, Fable 5.1 67,4%).

retained_facts.text: Anthropic is upgrading Claude Sonnet, replacing Sonnet 5 from June with Sonnet 5.5 as the best medium-sized model.
It’s a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5, runs more than 30% faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.
Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 is strongest at everyday tasks with a clear scope, including fixing bugs and creating polished documents, slides, and spreadsheets.
The company also highlights its design capabilities, from refining user interfaces to producing slides that follow templates and need minimal editing.
Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5’s pricing: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cache reads.
With cybersecurity capabilities comparable to Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 is the first Sonnet model to launch with cyber safeguards and fallbacks similar to those used for Anthropic’s most capable models.
